Definition: a prolonged form of an obsolete πλύω (to "flow"); to "plunge", i.e. launder clothing:--wash. Compare G3068, G3538.
BiblicalUsage: Plyno means to wash, to launder. The fishermen were washing their nets in Luke 5:2, and the multitude washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb in Revelation 7:14. Blessed are they that do His commandments, that they may wash their robes, says Revelation 22:14.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe nets and robes both need washing, and only the Lamb's blood makes either white.
